newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SA WEEK AHEAD-SAFRICA JUNE PPI SEEN SLIGHTLY LOWER.
newsitem.headline: SA WEEK AHEAD-SAFRICA JUNE PPI SEEN SLIGHTLY LOWER.

text.p: Benign local inflationary pressures and falling imported prices are expected to have nudged South African producer inflation slightly lower in June, economists said.

Reuter's consensus poll of 11 economists forecast the producer price index would rise 8.3 percent year-on-year or 0.5 percent month-on-month in June from 8.4 and 0.9 percent respectively in May. The data will be announced at 0900 GMT on Tuesday.
"We've seen in the last few months that local inflationary pressures have abated and it appears to be the trend," Rand Merchant Bank Treasury economist Julia Roy said.
"Imported inflation will probably be lower. It was up sharply last month on the oil imports and I wouldn't expect that to carry on," she added.
The imported component jumped 2.7 percent month-on-month in May, mainly as a result of a jump in crude petroleum prices.

"I think there is going to be a bit of an oil price decline...the diesel price started coming down and I think the rand's strength is still there so imported inflation will come down in June and might run through a bit to July," E.W. Balderson economist Mike Schussler said.
Edey Rogers economist Hugo Klein estimated that if one disregarded May's rise in petroleum prices, average producer inflation was rising at between 0.4 and 0.5 percent for the year.
"Import prices should continue to rise by about 1.0 percent and the rest of the economy is moving sideways," Klein said.
Barnard Jacobs Mellet economist Chantal Friedman noted, however, that crude oil prices actually fell in rand terms during the month.

"There was probably some pressure on food prices but it will be offset by a drop in the rand price of crude oil," she said, adding the fact that June was also a low survey month would also help the year-on-year average down.
